{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_e63ed12256ba413aae42e1e6","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# bead-forge (`bf`)\n2\t\n3\t![bead-forge hero](hero.png)\n4\t\n5\t**bead-forge** is a Rust CLI that replaces `br` (beads_rust) as the bead management tool for AI-supervised coding workflows. It is a drop-in replacement for `br` — every command, flag, and output format is identical — with one critical improvement: **concurrent claiming is correct**.\n6\t\n7\t---\n8\t\n9\t## The Problem It Solves\n10\t\n11\t`br` has a race condition at its core. Claiming a bead requires two separate operations:\n12\t\n13\t```\n14\tbr ready --json          # read candidates (snapshot)\n15\t  ↓  (race window)\n16\tbr update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <worker>\n17\t  ↓  (race window)\n18\tbr show <id>             # verify the claim stuck\n19\t```\n20\t\n21\tWith 20 NEEDLE workers running simultaneously, multiple workers read the same candidate list, all select the same top bead, and all issue `br update`. SQLite last-writer-wins — 19 workers hold phantom claims on beads they don't actually own.\n22\t\n23\t`bf` eliminates this with a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` SQLite transaction:\n24\t\n25\t```\n26\tbf claim --assignee worker-7 --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --json\n27\t```\n28\t\n29\tThe entire read-score-update sequence runs inside one write lock. No two workers can observe the same candidate state.\n30\t\n31\t---\n32\t\n33\t## Architecture\n34\t\n35\t```\n36\tSQLite (live store)                    issues.jsonl (git artifact)\n37\t    │                                        │\n38\t    │  all reads and writes                  │  exported by bf sync --flush\n39\t    │                                        │  imported by bf sync --import\n40\t    ▼                                        ▼\n41\t  beads.db                            .beads/issues.jsonl\n42\t  (gitignored)                        (committed to git)\n43\t```\n44\t\n45\t**SQLite is the live database.** JSONL is a derived snapshot committed to git for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. `beads.db` is rebuilt at any time with `bf doctor --repair`.\n46\t\n47\t**No daemon. No server. No flock.** Each `bf` invocation is self-contained: open DB, acquire write lock, execute, release, exit. SQLite WAL mode enables concurrent reads during writes.\n48\t\n49\t---\n50\t\n51\t## Key Features\n52\t\n53\t### Atomic Concurrent Claiming\n54\t\n55\t```\n56\tWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT + score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\n57\tWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked until Worker 1 commits) → SELECT → ...\n58\t...\n59\tWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT\n60\t```\n61\t\n62\tThe entire claim pipeline — stale reclamation, candidate scoring, winner selection, status update, event recording — runs in a single SQLite write transaction. Guaranteed correct under any concurrency level.\n63\t\n64\t### Critical Path Scoring\n65\t\n66\t`bf` computes the **float** of each bead: how many hops it can slip before delaying its epic. Beads on the critical path (`float == 0`) receive a 1000-point bonus in the claim scorer, ensuring the fleet works on the most impactful beads automatically — without human priority curation.\n67\t\n68\t```\n69\t$ bf critical-path bf-epic-123\n70\t\n71\t  float=0  [bf-a3f8] Implement auth token refresh        in_progress\n72\t  float=0  [bf-b2c1] Fix concurrent session state bug    open\n73\t  float=2  [bf-d5e3] Update API documentation            open\n74\t```\n75\t\n76\t### Velocity-Aware Scoring\n77\t\n78\tWorkers declare their composition when claiming:\n79\t\n80\t```bash\n81\tbf claim --assignee worker-7 \\\n82\t         --model claude-sonnet-4-6 \\\n83\t         --harness needle \\\n84\t         --harness-version 0.5.2 \\\n85\t         --json\n86\t```\n87\t\n88\t`bf` tracks close times per `(model, harness, issue_type)` in `velocity_stats`. The claim scorer weights candidates by `impact / expected_duration` — the fleet maximizes throughput per unit time, not just raw priority. After 10+ completions per cohort, routing becomes measurably smarter.\n89\t\n90\t```\n91\t$ bf velocity\n92\t\n93\tModel                  Harness   Type     Samples  p50    p90\n94\tclaude-opus-4-7        needle    task     142      8m     22m\n95\tclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    task     87       18m    45m\n96\tclaude-haiku-4-5       needle    task     23       35m    2h10m\n97\t```\n98\t\n99\t### Atomic Batch Operations\n100\t\n101\tReplaces NEEDLE's crash-unsafe create+dep chains:\n102\t\n103\t```bash\n104\t# NEEDLE mitosis: split 1 bead into N children atomically\n105\t# Method 1: Dedicated mitosis command (recommended)\n106\tbf mitosis bf-a3f8 \\\n107\t  --children '[\n108\t    {\"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2},\n109\t    {\"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2}\n110\t  ]' \\\n111\t  --reason \"Split into children\"\n112\t\n113\t# Method 2: Direct batch with placeholder references\n114\t# Use @0, @1, ... to reference beads created earlier in the batch\n115\tbf batch --json '[\n116\t  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n117\t  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n118\t  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@0\", \"child\": \"bf-a3f8\"},\n119\t  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@1\", \"child\": \"bf-a3f8\"},\n120\t  {\"op\": \"close\", \"id\": \"bf-a3f8\", \"reason\": \"Split into children\"}\n121\t]'\n122\t```\n123\t\n124\t**Placeholder references**: `@0`, `@1`, etc. resolve to the IDs of beads created earlier in the batch. You don't need to know the child IDs in advance — `bf` substitutes them automatically.\n125\t\n126\tAll operations execute in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. A crash mid-batch leaves zero partial state — SQLite rolls back automatically.\n127\t\n128\t### Extensible Annotations\n129\t\n130\tArbitrary key-value metadata on any bead, transparent to `br`:\n131\t\n132\t```bash\n133\tbf annotate set bf-a3f8 needle_attempt 3\n134\tbf annotate set bf-a3f8 needle_session abc123\n135\tbf annotate set bf-a3f8 review_status needs_review\n136\tbf list --annotation needle_attempt=3\n137\t```\n138\t\n139\t### Operation History\n140\t\n141\t```bash\n142\tbf log bf-a3f8\n143\t\n144\t2026-04-29 10:00  CREATED     by: human                  \"Implement auth flow\"\n145\t2026-04-29 14:30  CLAIMED     by: worker-3 (sonnet-4-6)  open → in_progress\n146\t2026-04-29 15:45  COMMENT     by: worker-3               \"Found edge case\"\n147\t2026-04-29 16:00  CLOSED      by: worker-3               \"Completed\"\n148\t```\n149\t\n150\t---\n151\t\n152\t### Secret Scanning (Pre-Commit Hook)\n153\t\n154\t`bf` scans for secrets before writing to the database (see `.beads/config.yaml` → `secret_protection`). The `bf commit-check` command extends this to git — it runs as a pre-commit hook to block commits that would add secrets to `.beads/` files.\n155\t\n156\t```bash\n157\t# Manual scan\n158\tbf commit-check\n159\t# Exits 0 (clean) or 1 (secrets found) with detailed error output\n160\t```\n161\t\n162\t**Installation as git pre-commit hook:**\n163\t\n164\t```bash\n165\t# In your workspace repo\n166\tcat > .git/hooks/pre-commit << 'EOF'\n167\t#!/bin/sh\n168\tbf commit-check\n169\tEOF\n170\t\n171\tchmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit\n172\t```\n173\t\n174\t**What gets scanned:**\n175\t- `.beads/config.yaml` — workspace configuration\n176\t- `.beads/metadata.json` — database path settings\n177\t- `.beads/issues.jsonl` — bead data (git artifact)\n178\t\n179\t**Patterns detected:**\n180\t- AWS keys (`AKIA...`, secret access keys)\n181\t- GitHub tokens (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `github_pat_`)\n182\t- Private keys (`BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY`, `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`)\n183\t- JWT tokens\n184\t- API keys in URLs\n185\t- Database connection strings\n186\t- And more (same scanner as write-time protection)\n187\t\n188\t**Allowlist exceptions:**\n189\t\n190\tIf a pattern is legitimately non-secret, add to `.beads/config.yaml`:\n191\t\n192\t```yaml\n193\tsecret_protection:\n194\t  allowlist:\n195\t    - \"^AKIAEXAMPLE$\"  # exact string\n196\t    - \"password: test\"  # substring\n197\t```\n198\t\n199\t---\n200\t\n201\t## Commands\n202\t\n203\tMost commands accept `--format json|text|toon` for output and a global `-w/--workspace <path>` to target a workspace other than the current directory. The global `--no-auto-flush` flag disables the post-mutation incremental JSONL export for that one invocation (mutations stay db-only and marked dirty until `bf sync --flush-only`); see [Auto-Flush](#auto-flush-phase-71--the-checkpoint-tracks-the-live-store) below.\n204\t\n205\t```\n206\t# ── Lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n207\tbf create        --title \"...\" [--type <t>] [--priority <N>] [--description \"...\"]\n208\t                 [--assignee <a>] [--label <l> ...]\n209\tbf list          [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>]\n210\t                 [--annotation k=v] [--limit <N>] [--all] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\n211\tbf show          <id> [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\n212\tbf update        <id> [--title \"...\"] [--status <s>] [--priority <N>] [--assignee <a>]\n213\t                 [--description \"...\"] [--description-file <path>] [--acceptance-criteria \"...\"]\n214\t                 [--notes \"...\"] [--design \"...\"] [--due-at <RFC3339>]\n215\tbf close         <id> [--reason \"...\"]\n216\tbf reopen        <id>\n217\tbf delete        <id>\n218\tbf ready         [--limit <N>] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]   # unblocked beads\n219\tbf count         [--status <s>]\n220\t\n221\t# ── Claiming & concurrency ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n222\tbf claim         --assignee <id> [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--harness-version <v>]\n223\t                 [--any] [--fallback <mode>] [--workspace-paths <p> ...] [--dry-run]\n224\t                 [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\n225\tbf batch         [--file ops.json] [--json '[...]'] [--stdin]       # atomic multi-op\n226\tbf mitosis       <id> --children '[...]' [--reason \"...\"] [--format ...]   # split into children\n227\t\n228\t# ── Dependencies & structure ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n229\tbf dep add       <blocker> --blocks <blocked> [-t <type>]   # blocker must close first\n230\tbf dep remove    <issue> <depends-on>\n231\tbf dep list      <id>\n232\tbf dep tree      <id> [-d down|up|both] [--max-depth <N>] [--format ...] [--json]\n233\tbf critical-path <epic-id> [--max-depth <N>] [--format ...]\n234\t\n235\t# ── Labels, comments, annotations ────────────────────────────────────────────\n236\tbf label add     --label <l> [<l> ...] <id>\n237\tbf label remove  --label <l> [<l> ...] <id>\n238\tbf label list    [<id>]                  # all unique labels if id omitted\n239\tbf labels        <id> [--format text|json]                  # efficient single-bead SELECT\n240\tbf comments add  <id> <text ...>\n241\tbf comments list <id>\n242\tbf annotate set    <id> <key> <value>\n243\tbf annotate get    <id> <key>\n244\tbf annotate remove <id> <key>\n245\tbf annotate list   <id>\n246\tbf annotate clear  <id>\n247\t\n248\t# ── Query & history ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n249\tbf search        [<query>] [-s <status> ...] [-t <type> ...] [--assignee <a>]\n250\t                 [-l <label> ...] [--priority-min <N>] [--priority-max <N>] [--limit <N>]\n251\t                 [--format json|text|toon]\n252\tbf recent        [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>]\n253\t                 [--since <RFC3339>] [--before <RFC3339>] [-t <period>] [-n <N>]\n254\t                 [--format json|text|toon] [--json]           # period: e.g. 1h, 24h, 7d, 4w\n255\tbf log           [<id>] [--limit <N>] [--since <RFC3339>] [--actor <a>]\n256\t                 [--status-changes] [--diff] [--git] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\n257\tbf stats         [--by-type] [--by-priority] [--by-assignee] [--by-label] [--format ...]\n258\tbf velocity      [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--format json|text|toon]\n259\t\n260\t# ── Maintenance & config ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n261\tbf sync          [--flush-only] [--import-only]\n262\tbf merge-jsonl   --ours <A> --theirs <B> [--base <O>] [--output <path>]  # 3-way JSONL merge / git driver\n263\tbf doctor        [--repair [--flush-first] [--force]] [--reclaim-stale [--ttl <minutes>]]  # no flags = health check\n264\tbf rotate        [--days <N>] [--dry-run]\n265\tbf migrate       [--workspace <p>] [--from-jsonl] [--seed-velocity] [--dry-run] [--skip-verify]\n266\tbf init          [--prefix <p>]\n267\tbf schema        [<target|id>] [--format json|text]      # \"all\" = DDL; a bead id = full JSON\n268\tbf config        list | get <key> | set <key> <value> | path\n269\tbf commit-check  # git pre-commit hook for secret scanning\n270\t```\n271\t\n272\tAll `br` commands work identically. `bf` is a strict superset.\n273\t\n274\t---\n275\t\n276\t## Output Formats\n277\t\n278\tMost read commands accept `--format text|json|toon` (or the `--json` alias for\n279\t`--format json`). The JSON shape depends on **which command** you run, and it is\n280\tnot always a JSON array.\n281\t\n282\t### Listing commands emit JSONL — not a JSON array\n283\t\n284\t`bf list`, `bf ready`, `bf search`, and `bf recent` with `--format json` emit\n285\t**JSONL**: one self-contained, compact JSON object per line, joined by newlines,\n286\twith **no array wrapper** and no commas between objects.\n287\t\n288\t```bash\n289\t$ bf list --format json\n290\t{\"id\":\"test-3qv\",\"title\":\"alpha task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,\"issue_type\":\"task\",\"assignee\":null,\"labels\":[],\"created_at\":\"2026-07-22T15:54:16Z\",...}\n291\t{\"id\":\"test-2c4\",\"title\":\"beta task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,\"issue_type\":\"task\",\"assignee\":null,\"labels\":[],\"created_at\":\"2026-07-22T15:54:16Z\",...}\n292\t```\n293\t\n294\tThe concatenated stdout is **not** valid JSON (`{\"a\":1}\\n{\"b\":2}` is two values,\n295\tnot one), so you cannot `json.loads()` the whole buffer. Parse it **line by\n296\tline**:\n297\t\n298\t```python\n299\timport json, subprocess\n300\tout = subprocess.check_output([\"bf\", \"list\", \"--format\", \"json\"], text=True)\n301\tbeads = [json.loads(line) for line in out.splitlines() if line.strip()]\n302\t```\n303\t\n304\t```bash\n305\t# jq: slurp the JSONL lines into one array, then operate on it\n306\tbf list --format json | jq -s 'map(.id)'\n307\t```\n308\t\n309\tTwo keys are **always** present on every emitted object, even on a bare bead:\n310\t\n311\t- `assignee` — `null` when unassigned (never omitted)\n312\t- `labels` — an array, `[]` when empty (never omitted)\n313\t\n314\tThe on-disk `issues.jsonl` checkpoint (written by `bf sync`) omits these when\n315\tunset to stay compact; the CLI `--format json` path normalizes them back so a\n316\tdownstream struct with non-optional `assignee`/`labels` fields deserializes\n317\tcleanly.\n318\t\n319\t**Empty results differ by command:**\n320\t\n321\t| Command | Empty `--format json` output |\n322\t|---------|------------------------------|\n323\t| `bf list` | nothing (empty stdout) |\n324\t| `bf search` / `bf recent` | nothing (empty stdout) |\n325\t| `bf ready` | `[]` |\n326\t\n327\t`ready` is the one listing command that special-cases emptiness to `[]`; the\n328\tothers print nothing at all.\n329\t\n330\t### `bf show` emits a one-element array\n331\t\n332\tUnlike the listing commands, `bf show <id> --format json` wraps the single bead\n333\tin a **JSON array of one element**:\n334\t\n335\t```bash\n336\t$ bf show test-3qv --format json\n337\t[{\"id\":\"test-3qv\",\"title\":\"alpha task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,...}]\n338\t```\n339\t\n340\tThis is deliberate: NEEDLE's `parse_single_bead` expects `Vec<Bead>` and takes\n341\tthe first element, so `show` ships an array to stay parse-compatible with that\n342\tcode path.\n343\t\n344\t### `bf claim` emits a single object\n345\t\n346\t`bf claim --json` prints one JSON object describing the claim (or `{}` when\n347\tnothing was claimed) — never an array, never an `Issue`:\n348\t\n349\t```bash\n350\t$ bf claim --assignee worker-7 --json\n351\t{\"bead_id\":\"test-3qv\",\"assignee\":\"worker-7\",\"reclaimed\":0}\n352\t```\n353\t\n354\t`bf velocity --format json` emits a JSON array of stat objects (`[]` when empty).\n355\t\n356\t### `br` produces byte-identical output\n357\t\n358\t`br` delegates to the `bf` binary — either directly (a symlink, as installed by\n359\t`ln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br`) or via a logging shim that writes a\n360\tdeprecation-telemetry line and then `exec bf \"$@\"`. Neither path touches stdout,\n361\tso every `br` command emits **byte-identical** output to its `bf` equivalent —\n362\tsame JSONL, same array wrapping for `show`, same empty-case behavior. A parser\n363\twritten for `br list --format json` works unchanged for `bf list --format json`,\n364\tand vice versa.\n365\t\n366\t---\n367\t\n368\t## NEEDLE Integration\n369\t\n370\tReplace the five non-atomic `br` chains in `bead_store/mod.rs`:\n371\t\n372\t| Old (racy) | New (atomic) |\n373\t|-----------|--------------|\n374\t| `br ready` → `br update` → `br show` (3 calls, 2 race windows) | `bf claim` (1 call, 1 transaction) |\n375\t| `br create` + `br dep add` (orphan if crash between) | `bf batch` (crash-safe, all-or-nothing) |\n376\t| `br show` just to get `.labels` field | `bf labels <id>` (direct `SELECT` on labels table) |\n377\t| N × `br label add` loops (N processes) | `bf label <id> add l1 l2 l3` (one transaction) |\n378\t\n379\tBackward compatibility — install `br` as a symlink:\n380\t\n381\t```bash\n382\tln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n383\t```\n384\t\n385\t---\n386\t\n387\t## Compatibility\n388\t\n389\t`bf` reads and writes the same SQLite schema and JSONL format as `br`. A workspace used by `bf` can be read by `br` and vice versa. Verified by three test suites (see plan §Compatibility Verification):\n390\t\n391\t1. **JSONL round-trip**: `br list --format json` == `bf list --format json` on the same workspace\n392\t2. **SQLite compat**: `bf` writes, `br` reads, `br doctor` passes\n393\t3. **Claim race**: 20 concurrent `bf claim` processes, 10 beads — exactly 10 claims succeed, no bead claimed twice\n394\t\n395\t---\n396\t\n397\t## Reliability\n398\t\n399\t- **rusqlite** (standard SQLite C library) — not FrankenSQLite, which had known corruption under concurrent writes\n400\t- **WAL mode** — concurrent reads never block writes; writers queue, not corrupt\n401\t- **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** — acquires write lock before any reads; eliminates TOCTOU\n402\t- **`SQLITE_BUSY` retry** — exponential backoff up to 5 retries; converts contention spikes to short waits\n403\t\n404\t### Data Authority Model\n405\t\n406\t**bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br**:\n407\t\n408\t| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n409\t|------|----------------|-----------------|\n410\t| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n411\t| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n412\t\n413\tThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. All mutations (create/update/claim) go to SQLite. With `sync.auto_flush` (default **on**), every successful mutation also incrementally exports the changed beads to `issues.jsonl`, so the checkpoint tracks the live store instead of trailing it — a separate flush is no longer needed in normal operation.\n414\t\n415\t### Auto-Flush (Phase 7.1) — the checkpoint tracks the live store\n416\t\n417\tWith `sync.auto_flush` (default **on**), every successful mutation (`create`/`update`/`claim`/`close`/`batch`) incrementally exports just the changed beads to `issues.jsonl` (a surgical line replacement, not a full rewrite). The JSONL artifact therefore stays current with SQLite after every command — no separate flush step is required in normal operation. Read-only and diagnostic commands never write the JSONL.\n418\t\n419\t```yaml\n420\t# .beads/config.yaml\n421\tsync:\n422\t  auto_flush: true     # default; set false to make mutations db-only until bf sync --flush-only\n423\t```\n424\t\n425\t```bash\n426\tbf create --title \"...\"               # auto-flushed by default → already in issues.jsonl\n427\tbf create --title \"...\" --no-auto-flush   # per-invocation override: db-only, marked dirty\n428\t```\n429\t\n430\t**Flush failure never fails the mutation.** Auto-flush is best-effort: if the incremental export fails, the mutation still commits, the dirty mark is retained, and the failure is surfaced loudly — a `warning:` line on stderr and a non-null `warning` field in the `--json` envelope naming the recovery command. The dirty bead stays recoverable.\n431\t\n432\t**Named recovery.** `bf sync --flush-only` is the explicit checkpoint and the recovery path: it clears the entire `dirty_issues` set and rewrites a **full** checkpoint (every bead, not just the dirty one). Run it after an auto-flush warning, or to produce a clean git-committable snapshot:\n433\t\n434\t```bash\n435\tbf sync --flush-only\n436\t```\n437\t\n438\t### Repair safety — protection is in the doctor, not a manual ritual\n439\t\n440\t`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from `issues.jsonl`. Because auto-flush keeps the checkpoint current, the old \"ALWAYS `bf sync --flush-only` before repair\" ritual (added after the 2026-06-10 incident where seven agents across seven workspaces each lost their first batch of fresh beads to a post-create `doctor --repair`; four db-only beads in ARMOR — bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44 — were permanently lost) is **obsolete**. The data-loss guard now lives in the doctor command itself: it **refuses** to repair when unflushed (db-only) beads exist, and tells you exactly what to do.\n441\t\n442\t```bash\n443\tbf doctor                              # health check — reports \"Unflushed beads: N\" if any\n444\tbf doctor --repair                     # REFUSES if unflushed beads exist (no data loss)\n445\tbf doctor --repair --flush-first       # checkpoint unflushed beads first, then rebuild\n446\tbf doctor --repair --force             # proceed anyway — unflushed beads WILL be lost\n447\t```\n448\t\n449\tKilling a worker at any point between mutation and flush loses nothing that `git diff .beads/` can't show: with auto-flush on the bead is already in the artifact when the command returns; with auto-flush off the bead survives in SQLite (marked dirty) and is recovered by `bf sync --flush-only`. Pinned by `tests/recovery_and_exit_criteria.rs`.\n450\t\n451\t### Multi-Box & Fleet Hardening (Phase 7.9)\n452\t\n453\tWhen the same repo is checked out on several boxes, each keeps its own live `beads.db` and shares state through the git-committed `issues.jsonl`. Three layers defend that shared artifact:\n454\t\n455\t**Three-way JSONL merge** — a plain git text merge of `issues.jsonl` is unsafe: each line is a whole bead, so a textual conflict marker corrupts JSON and \"take theirs\" silently drops beads. `bf merge-jsonl` merges **per-bead** against a common ancestor instead. Resolution is deterministic: a one-sided edit is taken as-is; a two-sided edit resolves last-writer-wins by `updated_at` (ties broken by content hash, so the result is independent of which box runs the merge); a delete that races a concurrent edit keeps the edit (never silently discards work). Wire it as a git merge driver:\n456\t\n457\t```bash\n458\tgit config merge.beads.name   \"bead-forge 3-way JSONL merge\"\n459\tgit config merge.beads.driver \"bf merge-jsonl --base %O --ours %A --theirs %B --output %A\"\n460\techo '.beads/issues.jsonl merge=beads' >> .gitattributes\n461\t```\n462\t\n463\t**Merge anchor** (`.beads/beads.base.jsonl`) — every full flush/import refreshes this snapshot of the last state this box agreed on with the artifact. It is the fallback three-way base for `bf merge-jsonl` when git does not supply `%O` (out-of-band merges across checkouts). Local-only; git-ignored.\n464\t\n465\t**Pre-export history backups** (`.beads/.bf_history/`) — before every full flush overwrites `issues.jsonl`, the previous version is copied into `.bf_history/` and pruned to the newest `history.max_backups` snapshots (default 20). One more recovery layer under a bad export or merge. Enabled by default; disable with `history.enabled: false` in `config.yaml`. Local-only; git-ignored.\n466\t\n467\t**Fleet concurrency tests** (`tests/fleet_concurrency.rs`) — spawn N concurrent `bf` *processes* doing create/claim/close and assert the upstream bug classes stay dead: no parallel-write silent loss (`count` equals successful creates), no loss across flush + fresh-DB reimport, and no bead claimed twice under a 20-worker herd on 15 beads.\n468\t\n469\t---\n470\t\n471\t## Implementation\n472\t\n473\tSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](plan/plan.md) for the complete implementation plan including:\n474\t\n475\t- Exact SQLite schema (all 13 tables + indexes)\n476\t- `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` retry wrapper implementation\n477\t- Critical path CTE algorithm\n478\t- Velocity stats schema and claim scoring formula\n479\t- Compatibility verification test suites\n480\t- NEEDLE integration specifics (file, line numbers, before/after)\n481\t\n482\t---\n483\t\n484\t## Migration from br to bf\n485\t\n486\t### Output Format Compatibility (no parser changes)\n487\t\n488\tMigrating to `bf` requires **no changes to JSON consumers**. `bf` is a drop-in\n489\treplacement: every command emits byte-identical output to `br`, because `br`\n490\tdelegates to the `bf` binary (via symlink, or a logging shim that `exec bf\n491\t\"$@\"`) and never alters stdout.\n492\t\n493\tThe format to keep in mind (full details in [§ Output Formats](#output-formats)):\n494\t\n495\t- `list` / `ready` / `search` / `recent --format json` → **JSONL** (one object\n496\t  per line, not a JSON array). It is a drop-in replacement for `br` — every command, flag, and output format is identical — with one critical improvement: **concurrent claiming is correct**.\n\n---\n\n## The Problem It Solves\n\n`br` has a race condition at its core. Claiming a bead requires two separate operations:\n\n```\nbr ready --json          # read candidates (snapshot)\n  ↓  (race window)\nbr update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <worker>\n  ↓  (race window)\nbr show <id>             # verify the claim stuck\n```\n\nWith 20 NEEDLE workers running simultaneously, multiple workers read the same candidate list, all select the same top bead, and all issue `br update`. SQLite last-writer-wins — 19 workers hold phantom claims on beads they don't actually own.\n\n`bf` eliminates this with a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` SQLite transaction:\n\n```\nbf claim --assignee worker-7 --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --json\n```\n\nThe entire read-score-update sequence runs inside one write lock. No two workers can observe the same candidate state.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\nSQLite (live store)                    issues.jsonl (git artifact)\n    │                                        │\n    │  all reads and writes                  │  exported by bf sync --flush\n    │                                        │  imported by bf sync --import\n    ▼                                        ▼\n  beads.db                            .beads/issues.jsonl\n  (gitignored)                        (committed to git)\n```\n\n**SQLite is the live database.** JSONL is a derived snapshot committed to git for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. `beads.db` is rebuilt at any time with `bf doctor --repair`.\n\n**No daemon. No server. No flock.** Each `bf` invocation is self-contained: open DB, acquire write lock, execute, release, exit. SQLite WAL mode enables concurrent reads during writes.\n\n---\n\n## Key Features\n\n### Atomic Concurrent Claiming\n\n```\nWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT + score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\nWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked until Worker 1 commits) → SELECT → ...\n...\nWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT\n```\n\nThe entire claim pipeline — stale reclamation, candidate scoring, winner selection, status update, event recording — runs in a single SQLite write transaction. Guaranteed correct under any concurrency level.\n\n### Critical Path Scoring\n\n`bf` computes the **float** of each bead: how many hops it can slip before delaying its epic. Beads on the critical path (`float == 0`) receive a 1000-point bonus in the claim scorer, ensuring the fleet works on the most impactful beads automatically — without human priority curation.\n\n```\n$ bf critical-path bf-epic-123\n\n  float=0  [bf-a3f8] Implement auth token refresh        in_progress\n  float=0  [bf-b2c1] Fix concurrent session state bug    open\n  float=2  [bf-d5e3] Update API documentation            open\n```\n\n### Velocity-Aware Scoring\n\nWorkers declare their composition when claiming:\n\n```bash\nbf claim --assignee worker-7 \\\n         --model claude-sonnet-4-6 \\\n         --harness needle \\\n         --harness-version 0.5.2 \\\n         --json\n```\n\n`bf` tracks close times per `(model, harness, issue_type)` in `velocity_stats`. The claim scorer weights candidates by `impact / expected_duration` — the fleet maximizes throughput per unit time, not just raw priority. After 10+ completions per cohort, routing becomes measurably smarter.\n\n```\n$ bf velocity\n\nModel                  Harness   Type     Samples  p50    p90\nclaude-opus-4-7        needle    task     142      8m     22m\nclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    task     87       18m    45m\nclaude-haiku-4-5       needle    task     23       35m    2h10m\n```\n\n### Atomic Batch Operations\n\nReplaces NEEDLE's crash-unsafe create+dep chains:\n\n```bash\n# NEEDLE mitosis: split 1 bead into N children atomically\n# Method 1: Dedicated mitosis command (recommended)\nbf mitosis bf-a3f8 \\\n  --children '[\n    {\"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2},\n    {\"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2}\n  ]' \\\n  --reason \"Split into children\"\n\n# Method 2: Direct batch with placeholder references\n# Use @0, @1, ... to reference beads created earlier in the batch\nbf batch --json '[\n  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@0\", \"child\": \"bf-a3f8\"},\n  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@1\", \"child\": \"bf-a3f8\"},\n  {\"op\": \"close\", \"id\": \"bf-a3f8\", \"reason\": \"Split into children\"}\n]'\n```\n\n**Placeholder references**: `@0`, `@1`, etc. resolve to the IDs of beads created earlier in the batch. You don't need to know the child IDs in advance — `bf` substitutes them automatically.\n\nAll operations execute in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. A crash mid-batch leaves zero partial state — SQLite rolls back automatically.\n\n### Extensible Annotations\n\nArbitrary key-value metadata on any bead, transparent to `br`:\n\n```bash\nbf annotate set bf-a3f8 needle_attempt 3\nbf annotate set bf-a3f8 needle_session abc123\nbf annotate set bf-a3f8 review_status needs_review\nbf list --annotation needle_attempt=3\n```\n\n### Operation History\n\n```bash\nbf log bf-a3f8\n\n2026-04-29 10:00  CREATED     by: human                  \"Implement auth flow\"\n2026-04-29 14:30  CLAIMED     by: worker-3 (sonnet-4-6)  open → in_progress\n2026-04-29 15:45  COMMENT     by: worker-3               \"Found edge case\"\n2026-04-29 16:00  CLOSED      by: worker-3               \"Completed\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### Secret Scanning (Pre-Commit Hook)\n\n`bf` scans for secrets before writing to the database (see `.beads/config.yaml` → `secret_protection`). The `bf commit-check` command extends this to git — it runs as a pre-commit hook to block commits that would add secrets to `.beads/` files.\n\n```bash\n# Manual scan\nbf commit-check\n# Exits 0 (clean) or 1 (secrets found) with detailed error output\n```\n\n**Installation as git pre-commit hook:**\n\n```bash\n# In your workspace repo\ncat > .git/hooks/pre-commit << 'EOF'\n#!/bin/sh\nbf commit-check\nEOF\n\nchmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit\n```\n\n**What gets scanned:**\n- `.beads/config.yaml` — workspace configuration\n- `.beads/metadata.json` — database path settings\n- `.beads/issues.jsonl` — bead data (git artifact)\n\n**Patterns detected:**\n- AWS keys (`AKIA...`, secret access keys)\n- GitHub tokens (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `github_pat_`)\n- Private keys (`BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY`, `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`)\n- JWT tokens\n- API keys in URLs\n- Database connection strings\n- And more (same scanner as write-time protection)\n\n**Allowlist exceptions:**\n\nIf a pattern is legitimately non-secret, add to `.beads/config.yaml`:\n\n```yaml\nsecret_protection:\n  allowlist:\n    - \"^AKIAEXAMPLE$\"  # exact string\n    - \"password: test\"  # substring\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commands\n\nMost commands accept `--format json|text|toon` for output and a global `-w/--workspace <path>` to target a workspace other than the current directory. The global `--no-auto-flush` flag disables the post-mutation incremental JSONL export for that one invocation (mutations stay db-only and marked dirty until `bf sync --flush-only`); see [Auto-Flush](#auto-flush-phase-71--the-checkpoint-tracks-the-live-store) below.\n\n```\n# ── Lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf create        --title \"...\" [--type <t>] [--priority <N>] [--description \"...\"]\n                 [--assignee <a>] [--label <l> ...]\nbf list          [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>]\n                 [--annotation k=v] [--limit <N>] [--all] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\nbf show          <id> [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\nbf update        <id> [--title \"...\"] [--status <s>] [--priority <N>] [--assignee <a>]\n                 [--description \"...\"] [--description-file <path>] [--acceptance-criteria \"...\"]\n                 [--notes \"...\"] [--design \"...\"] [--due-at <RFC3339>]\nbf close         <id> [--reason \"...\"]\nbf reopen        <id>\nbf delete        <id>\nbf ready         [--limit <N>] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]   # unblocked beads\nbf count         [--status <s>]\n\n# ── Claiming & concurrency ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf claim         --assignee <id> [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--harness-version <v>]\n                 [--any] [--fallback <mode>] [--workspace-paths <p> ...] [--dry-run]\n                 [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\nbf batch         [--file ops.json] [--json '[...]'] [--stdin]       # atomic multi-op\nbf mitosis       <id> --children '[...]' [--reason \"...\"] [--format ...]   # split into children\n\n# ── Dependencies & structure ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf dep add       <blocker> --blocks <blocked> [-t <type>]   # blocker must close first\nbf dep remove    <issue> <depends-on>\nbf dep list      <id>\nbf dep tree      <id> [-d down|up|both] [--max-depth <N>] [--format ...] [--json]\nbf critical-path <epic-id> [--max-depth <N>] [--format ...]\n\n# ── Labels, comments, annotations ────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf label add     --label <l> [<l> ...] <id>\nbf label remove  --label <l> [<l> ...] <id>\nbf label list    [<id>]                  # all unique labels if id omitted\nbf labels        <id> [--format text|json]                  # efficient single-bead SELECT\nbf comments add  <id> <text ...>\nbf comments list <id>\nbf annotate set    <id> <key> <value>\nbf annotate get    <id> <key>\nbf annotate remove <id> <key>\nbf annotate list   <id>\nbf annotate clear  <id>\n\n# ── Query & history ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf search        [<query>] [-s <status> ...] [-t <type> ...] [--assignee <a>]\n                 [-l <label> ...] [--priority-min <N>] [--priority-max <N>] [--limit <N>]\n                 [--format json|text|toon]\nbf recent        [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>]\n                 [--since <RFC3339>] [--before <RFC3339>] [-t <period>] [-n <N>]\n                 [--format json|text|toon] [--json]           # period: e.g. 1h, 24h, 7d, 4w\nbf log           [<id>] [--limit <N>] [--since <RFC3339>] [--actor <a>]\n                 [--status-changes] [--diff] [--git] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\nbf stats         [--by-type] [--by-priority] [--by-assignee] [--by-label] [--format ...]\nbf velocity      [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--format json|text|toon]\n\n# ── Maintenance & config ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf sync          [--flush-only] [--import-only]\nbf merge-jsonl   --ours <A> --theirs <B> [--base <O>] [--output <path>]  # 3-way JSONL merge / git driver\nbf doctor        [--repair [--flush-first] [--force]] [--reclaim-stale [--ttl <minutes>]]  # no flags = health check\nbf rotate        [--days <N>] [--dry-run]\nbf migrate       [--workspace <p>] [--from-jsonl] [--seed-velocity] [--dry-run] [--skip-verify]\nbf init          [--prefix <p>]\nbf schema        [<target|id>] [--format json|text]      # \"all\" = DDL; a bead id = full JSON\nbf config        list | get <key> | set <key> <value> | path\nbf commit-check  # git pre-commit hook for secret scanning\n```\n\nAll `br` commands work identically. `bf` is a strict superset.\n\n---\n\n## Output Formats\n\nMost read commands accept `--format text|json|toon` (or the `--json` alias for\n`--format json`). The JSON shape depends on **which command** you run, and it is\nnot always a JSON array.\n\n### Listing commands emit JSONL — not a JSON array\n\n`bf list`, `bf ready`, `bf search`, and `bf recent` with `--format json` emit\n**JSONL**: one self-contained, compact JSON object per line, joined by newlines,\nwith **no array wrapper** and no commas between objects.\n\n```bash\n$ bf list --format json\n{\"id\":\"test-3qv\",\"title\":\"alpha task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,\"issue_type\":\"task\",\"assignee\":null,\"labels\":[],\"created_at\":\"2026-07-22T15:54:16Z\",...}\n{\"id\":\"test-2c4\",\"title\":\"beta task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,\"issue_type\":\"task\",\"assignee\":null,\"labels\":[],\"created_at\":\"2026-07-22T15:54:16Z\",...}\n```\n\nThe concatenated stdout is **not** valid JSON (`{\"a\":1}\\n{\"b\":2}` is two values,\nnot one), so you cannot `json.loads()` the whole buffer. Parse it **line by\nline**:\n\n```python\nimport json, subprocess\nout = subprocess.check_output([\"bf\", \"list\", \"--format\", \"json\"], text=True)\nbeads = [json.loads(line) for line in out.splitlines() if line.strip()]\n```\n\n```bash\n# jq: slurp the JSONL lines into one array, then operate on it\nbf list --format json | jq -s 'map(.id)'\n```\n\nTwo keys are **always** present on every emitted object, even on a bare bead:\n\n- `assignee` — `null` when unassigned (never omitted)\n- `labels` — an array, `[]` when empty (never omitted)\n\nThe on-disk `issues.jsonl` checkpoint (written by `bf sync`) omits these when\nunset to stay compact; the CLI `--format json` path normalizes them back so a\ndownstream struct with non-optional `assignee`/`labels` fields deserializes\ncleanly.\n\n**Empty results differ by command:**\n\n| Command | Empty `--format json` output |\n|---------|------------------------------|\n| `bf list` | nothing (empty stdout) |\n| `bf search` / `bf recent` | nothing (empty stdout) |\n| `bf ready` | `[]` |\n\n`ready` is the one listing command that special-cases emptiness to `[]`; the\nothers print nothing at all.\n\n### `bf show` emits a one-element array\n\nUnlike the listing commands, `bf show <id> --format json` wraps the single bead\nin a **JSON array of one element**:\n\n```bash\n$ bf show test-3qv --format json\n[{\"id\":\"test-3qv\",\"title\":\"alpha task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,...}]\n```\n\nThis is deliberate: NEEDLE's `parse_single_bead` expects `Vec<Bead>` and takes\nthe first element, so `show` ships an array to stay parse-compatible with that\ncode path.\n\n### `bf claim` emits a single object\n\n`bf claim --json` prints one JSON object describing the claim (or `{}` when\nnothing was claimed) — never an array, never an `Issue`:\n\n```bash\n$ bf claim --assignee worker-7 --json\n{\"bead_id\":\"test-3qv\",\"assignee\":\"worker-7\",\"reclaimed\":0}\n```\n\n`bf velocity --format json` emits a JSON array of stat objects (`[]` when empty).\n\n### `br` produces byte-identical output\n\n`br` delegates to the `bf` binary — either directly (a symlink, as installed by\n`ln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br`) or via a logging shim that writes a\ndeprecation-telemetry line and then `exec bf \"$@\"`. Neither path touches stdout,\nso every `br` command emits **byte-identical** output to its `bf` equivalent —\nsame JSONL, same array wrapping for `show`, same empty-case behavior. A parser\nwritten for `br list --format json` works unchanged for `bf list --format json`,\nand vice versa.\n\n---\n\n## NEEDLE Integration\n\nReplace the five non-atomic `br` chains in `bead_store/mod.rs`:\n\n| Old (racy) | New (atomic) |\n|-----------|--------------|\n| `br ready` → `br update` → `br show` (3 calls, 2 race windows) | `bf claim` (1 call, 1 transaction) |\n| `br create` + `br dep add` (orphan if crash between) | `bf batch` (crash-safe, all-or-nothing) |\n| `br show` just to get `.labels` field | `bf labels <id>` (direct `SELECT` on labels table) |\n| N × `br label add` loops (N processes) | `bf label <id> add l1 l2 l3` (one transaction) |\n\nBackward compatibility — install `br` as a symlink:\n\n```bash\nln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n```\n\n---\n\n## Compatibility\n\n`bf` reads and writes the same SQLite schema and JSONL format as `br`. A workspace used by `bf` can be read by `br` and vice versa. Verified by three test suites (see plan §Compatibility Verification):\n\n1. **JSONL round-trip**: `br list --format json` == `bf list --format json` on the same workspace\n2. **SQLite compat**: `bf` writes, `br` reads, `br doctor` passes\n3. **Claim race**: 20 concurrent `bf claim` processes, 10 beads — exactly 10 claims succeed, no bead claimed twice\n\n---\n\n## Reliability\n\n- **rusqlite** (standard SQLite C library) — not FrankenSQLite, which had known corruption under concurrent writes\n- **WAL mode** — concurrent reads never block writes; writers queue, not corrupt\n- **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** — acquires write lock before any reads; eliminates TOCTOU\n- **`SQLITE_BUSY` retry** — exponential backoff up to 5 retries; converts contention spikes to short waits\n\n### Data Authority Model\n\n**bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br**:\n\n| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n|------|----------------|-----------------|\n| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n\nThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. All mutations (create/update/claim) go to SQLite. With `sync.auto_flush` (default **on**), every successful mutation also incrementally exports the changed beads to `issues.jsonl`, so the checkpoint tracks the live store instead of trailing it — a separate flush is no longer needed in normal operation.\n\n### Auto-Flush (Phase 7.1) — the checkpoint tracks the live store\n\nWith `sync.auto_flush` (default **on**), every successful mutation (`create`/`update`/`claim`/`close`/`batch`) incrementally exports just the changed beads to `issues.jsonl` (a surgical line replacement, not a full rewrite). The JSONL artifact therefore stays current with SQLite after every command — no separate flush step is required in normal operation. Read-only and diagnostic commands never write the JSONL.\n\n```yaml\n# .beads/config.yaml\nsync:\n  auto_flush: true     # default; set false to make mutations db-only until bf sync --flush-only\n```\n\n```bash\nbf create --title \"...\"               # auto-flushed by default → already in issues.jsonl\nbf create --title \"...\" --no-auto-flush   # per-invocation override: db-only, marked dirty\n```\n\n**Flush failure never fails the mutation.** Auto-flush is best-effort: if the incremental export fails, the mutation still commits, the dirty mark is retained, and the failure is surfaced loudly — a `warning:` line on stderr and a non-null `warning` field in the `--json` envelope naming the recovery command. The dirty bead stays recoverable.\n\n**Named recovery.** `bf sync --flush-only` is the explicit checkpoint and the recovery path: it clears the entire `dirty_issues` set and rewrites a **full** checkpoint (every bead, not just the dirty one). Run it after an auto-flush warning, or to produce a clean git-committable snapshot:\n\n```bash\nbf sync --flush-only\n```\n\n### Repair safety — protection is in the doctor, not a manual ritual\n\n`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from `issues.jsonl`. Because auto-flush keeps the checkpoint current, the old \"ALWAYS `bf sync --flush-only` before repair\" ritual (added after the 2026-06-10 incident where seven agents across seven workspaces each lost their first batch of fresh beads to a post-create `doctor --repair`; four db-only beads in ARMOR — bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44 — were permanently lost) is **obsolete**. The data-loss guard now lives in the doctor command itself: it **refuses** to repair when unflushed (db-only) beads exist, and tells you exactly what to do.\n\n```bash\nbf doctor                              # health check — reports \"Unflushed beads: N\" if any\nbf doctor --repair                     # REFUSES if unflushed beads exist (no data loss)\nbf doctor --repair --flush-first       # checkpoint unflushed beads first, then rebuild\nbf doctor --repair --force             # proceed anyway — unflushed beads WILL be lost\n```\n\nKilling a worker at any point between mutation and flush loses nothing that `git diff .beads/` can't show: with auto-flush on the bead is already in the artifact when the command returns; with auto-flush off the bead survives in SQLite (marked dirty) and is recovered by `bf sync --flush-only`. Pinned by `tests/recovery_and_exit_criteria.rs`.\n\n### Multi-Box & Fleet Hardening (Phase 7.9)\n\nWhen the same repo is checked out on several boxes, each keeps its own live `beads.db` and shares state through the git-committed `issues.jsonl`. Three layers defend that shared artifact:\n\n**Three-way JSONL merge** — a plain git text merge of `issues.jsonl` is unsafe: each line is a whole bead, so a textual conflict marker corrupts JSON and \"take theirs\" silently drops beads. `bf merge-jsonl` merges **per-bead** against a common ancestor instead. Resolution is deterministic: a one-sided edit is taken as-is; a two-sided edit resolves last-writer-wins by `updated_at` (ties broken by content hash, so the result is independent of which box runs the merge); a delete that races a concurrent edit keeps the edit (never silently discards work). Wire it as a git merge driver:\n\n```bash\ngit config merge.beads.name   \"bead-forge 3-way JSONL merge\"\ngit config merge.beads.driver \"bf merge-jsonl --base %O --ours %A --theirs %B --output %A\"\necho '.beads/issues.jsonl merge=beads' >> .gitattributes\n```\n\n**Merge anchor** (`.beads/beads.base.jsonl`) — every full flush/import refreshes this snapshot of the last state this box agreed on with the artifact. It is the fallback three-way base for `bf merge-jsonl` when git does not supply `%O` (out-of-band merges across checkouts). Local-only; git-ignored.\n\n**Pre-export history backups** (`.beads/.bf_history/`) — before every full flush overwrites `issues.jsonl`, the previous version is copied into `.bf_history/` and pruned to the newest `history.max_backups` snapshots (default 20). One more recovery layer under a bad export or merge. Enabled by default; disable with `history.enabled: false` in `config.yaml`. Local-only; git-ignored.\n\n**Fleet concurrency tests** (`tests/fleet_concurrency.rs`) — spawn N concurrent `bf` *processes* doing create/claim/close and assert the upstream bug classes stay dead: no parallel-write silent loss (`count` equals successful creates), no loss across flush + fresh-DB reimport, and no bead claimed twice under a 20-worker herd on 15 beads.\n\n---\n\n## Implementation\n\nSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](plan/plan.md) for the complete implementation plan including:\n\n- Exact SQLite schema (all 13 tables + indexes)\n- `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` retry wrapper implementation\n- Critical path CTE algorithm\n- Velocity stats schema and claim scoring formula\n- Compatibility verification test suites\n- NEEDLE integration specifics (file, line numbers, before/after)\n\n---\n\n## Migration from br to bf\n\n### Output Format Compatibility (no parser changes)\n\nMigrating to `bf` requires **no changes to JSON consumers**. `bf` is a drop-in\nreplacement: every command emits byte-identical output to `br`, because `br`\ndelegates to the `bf` binary (via symlink, or a logging shim that `exec bf\n\"$@\"`) and never alters stdout.\n\nThe format to keep in mind (full details in [§ Output Formats](#output-formats)):\n\n- `list` / `ready` / `search` / `recent --format json` → **JSONL** (one object\n  per line, not a JSON array). Parse line-by-line — do not `json.loads()` the\n  whole buffer.\n- `show <id> --format json` → a **one-element array** (for NEEDLE's\n  `parse_single_bead`).\n- Empty `list`/`search`/`recent` print nothing; empty `ready` prints `[]`.\n\nAny script that already parses `br list --format json` line-by-line keeps\nworking unchanged against `bf`.\n\n### Per-Machine Installation\n\n```bash\n# Install bf binary\ncurl -L https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest/download/bf-linux-x86_64 \\\n  -o ~/.local/bin/bf && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n\n# Drop-in replace br (all existing scripts work unchanged)\nln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n\n# Verify installation\nbf --version\nbr --version  # should show same version\n```\n\n### Per-Workspace Migration\n\n**Standard migration** (Path B: explicit, with backup and verification):\n\n```bash\n# Migrate a single workspace\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace\n\n# Or migrate all workspaces in a loop\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  bf migrate --workspace \"$workspace\"\ndone\n```\n\n**What `bf migrate` does:**\n1. Acquires migration lock (prevents concurrent claims during migration)\n2. Backs up `beads.db` → `beads.db.br-backup-<timestamp>`\n3. Applies schema migrations (creates bf-only tables via `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`)\n4. Primes critical_path_cache for all epics\n5. Seeds `config.yaml` with bf-specific defaults if missing\n6. Verifies forward compatibility (br can still open the database)\n7. Verifies backward compatibility (`bf doctor` health check passes)\n8. Releases migration lock\n\n**Dry-run mode** (see what would happen without making changes):\n\n```bash\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace --dry-run\n```\n\n**Recovery mode** (for corrupted/missing databases):\n\nIf `beads.db` is corrupted or missing, `bf migrate --from-jsonl` rebuilds from `issues.jsonl` and reconstructs events from git history:\n\n```bash\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace --from-jsonl [--seed-velocity]\n```\n\n### Migration Checklist\n\n**Step 1: Per-machine installation**\n\n```bash\n# Install bf binary\ncurl -L https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest/download/bf-linux-x86_64 \\\n  -o ~/.local/bin/bf && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n\n# Drop-in replace br (all existing scripts work unchanged)\nln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n\n# Verify installation\nbf --version\nbr --version  # should show same version\n```\n\n**Step 2: Per-workspace migration loop**\n\n```bash\n# Migrate all workspaces\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  echo \"Migrating $workspace...\"\n  bf migrate --workspace \"$workspace\"\ndone\n```\n\n**Step 3: Verify each migration**\n\n```bash\n# Verify each workspace passes both doctor checks\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  echo \"Checking $workspace...\"\n  cd \"$workspace\" || continue\n  echo \"  bf doctor:\"\n  bf doctor || echo \"  ❌ bf doctor failed\"\n  echo \"  br doctor:\"\n  br doctor || echo \"  ❌ br doctor failed\"\ndone\n```\n\nBoth `bf doctor` and `br doctor` should exit 0 with no errors for each workspace.\n\n**Step 4: Update NEEDLE adapter configs**\n\nAfter migration, update NEEDLE adapter configs to pass worker metadata for velocity tracking:\n\n```yaml\n# In .config/needle/adapters/claude-sonnet.yaml, update invoke_template:\nbf claim --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --harness-version 0.5.2 ...\n```\n\nThis enables velocity-aware routing (see §Velocity-Aware Scoring above).\n\n### Verification After Migration\n\nFor each workspace, verify both tools can read the database:\n\n```bash\n# Verify bf doctor passes (no flags = health check)\ncd /path/to/workspace\nbf doctor\n\n# Verify br doctor passes (forward compatibility)\nbr doctor\n```\n\nBoth commands should exit 0 with no errors.\n\n**Known limitation:** The migration may show a forward compatibility warning: \"Forward compatibility check failed: issues table column count mismatch\". The database is fully consistent when this occurs. The retry converts a transient contention spike (e.g., 20 workers all starting within the same millisecond) into a short wait rather than a user-visible error.\n238\t\n239\t**All write operations** (`claim`, `create`, `update`, `close`, `batch`) use `with_immediate_transaction`. Read-only operations (`list`, `show`, `ready`) use a plain `BEGIN DEFERRED` transaction and are never affected by write contention.\n240\t\n241\t### 2.7 Doctor/Repair (`src/doctor.rs`)\n242\t\n243\t- `doctor --repair`: Delete `beads.db`, reimport from JSONL\n244\t- `doctor --check`: Validate JSONL line integrity, check SQLite <-> JSONL consistency\n245\t- `doctor --repair --flush-first`: Flush unflushed beads to JSONL before repairing (protects against data loss)\n246\t- `doctor --repair --force`: Force repair even with unflushed beads (WARNING: unflushed beads are lost)\n247\t- **Flush-before-repair rule**: Always run `bf sync --flush-only` before `bf doctor --repair` to protect against losing unflushed beads\n248\t- Recovery from corruption: JSONL export is the authoritative checkpoint for recovery — `beads.db` can be rebuilt from it at any time\n249\t\n250\t**CRITICAL DATA AUTHORITY NOTE**: bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br:\n251\t\n252\t| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n253\t|------|----------------|-----------------|\n254\t| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n255\t| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n256\t\n257\tThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. **Beads created or modified since the last `bf sync --flush-only` exist only in SQLite**. Running `bf doctor --repair` without flushing first destroys these unflushed beads.\n258\t\n259\t**Historical context**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces (ARMOR, NEEDLE, AgentScribe, kalshi-weather, jedarden.com, vibe-coding-discovery, face/pose/sun repos) each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads in ARMOR (bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44) were permanently lost. This fix implements the flush-before-repair protection.\n260\t\n261\t---\n262\t\n263\t## Phase 3: CLI Commands\n264\t\n265\t### 3.1 Command Structure (`src/cli/`)\n266\t\n267\tUse `clap` with derive macros. Binary name: `bf`. Subcommands mirror br exactly.\n268\t\n269\t```\n270\tbf create    --title \"...\" --type <type> --priority <N> [--description \"...\"] [--label ...]\n271\tbf list      [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--limit N] [--format json|text|toon]\n272\tbf show      <id>\n273\tbf update    <id> [--status <s>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>] [--title \"...\"] ...\n274\tbf close     <id> [--reason \"...\"]\n275\tbf reopen    <id>\n276\tbf delete    <id>\n277\tbf ready         [--limit N]                     # Locate `.beads/` directory (walk up from CWD)\n317\t2. Load config + metadata\n318\t3. Open SQLite (`beads.db`), apply schema if new\n319\t4. Execute: mutations are SQL writes; reads are SQL queries\n320\t5. `bf sync` is the only command that touches `issues.jsonl` — flush exports it, import reads it\n321\t\n322\t### 3.4 Assignee Clearing Semantics (`--assignee \"\"` means unassigned, never an error)\n323\t\n324\t**Correct behavior (br parity):** an empty or whitespace-only `--assignee` value passed to `bf create` or `bf update` means \"no assignee\" / \"clear the assignee\" — it must never be rejected. `src/storage/sqlite.rs::update_issue` already implements this correctly:\n325\t\n326\t```rust\n327\tif let Some(ref assignee) = changes.assignee {\n328\t    if assignee.trim().is_empty() {\n329\t        // Clearing stores NULL, never an empty string that would\n330\t        // read back as \"assigned\" and hide the bead from claiming.\n331\t        updates.push(\"assignee = NULL\");\n332\t    } else {\n333\t        updates.push(\"assignee = ?\");\n334\t        params.push(Box::new(assignee.clone()));\n335\t    }\n336\t}\n337\t```\n338\t\n339\t**Known bug (currently live, blocking downstream consumers — fix tracked as bf-gj673, children bf-4mj7l and bf-2uhsk):** `src/cli/mod.rs`'s `cmd_create` and `cmd_update` both call `validate_assignee()` (`src/validation.rs`) *before* reaching the correct storage-layer logic above, and `validate_assignee()` still rejects empty/whitespace-only values with `Error: Assignee cannot be empty or whitespace-only`. This means the correct clear-on-empty behavior is currently unreachable via the CLI — `bf update <id> --assignee \"\"` fails outright instead of clearing the field.\n340\t\n341\t- `validate_assignee()` was added by bf-2nrol (closed) per an earlier, since-superseded design (\"assignee must be non-empty when provided\"). The database is fully consistent when this occurs. The retry converts a transient contention spike (e.g., 20 workers all starting within the same millisecond) into a short wait rather than a user-visible error.\n\n**All write operations** (`claim`, `create`, `update`, `close`, `batch`) use `with_immediate_transaction`. Read-only operations (`list`, `show`, `ready`) use a plain `BEGIN DEFERRED` transaction and are never affected by write contention.\n\n### 2.7 Doctor/Repair (`src/doctor.rs`)\n\n- `doctor --repair`: Delete `beads.db`, reimport from JSONL\n- `doctor --check`: Validate JSONL line integrity, check SQLite <-> JSONL consistency\n- `doctor --repair --flush-first`: Flush unflushed beads to JSONL before repairing (protects against data loss)\n- `doctor --repair --force`: Force repair even with unflushed beads (WARNING: unflushed beads are lost)\n- **Flush-before-repair rule**: Always run `bf sync --flush-only` before `bf doctor --repair` to protect against losing unflushed beads\n- Recovery from corruption: JSONL export is the authoritative checkpoint for recovery — `beads.db` can be rebuilt from it at any time\n\n**CRITICAL DATA AUTHORITY NOTE**: bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br:\n\n| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n|------|----------------|-----------------|\n| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n\nThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. **Beads created or modified since the last `bf sync --flush-only` exist only in SQLite**. Running `bf doctor --repair` without flushing first destroys these unflushed beads.\n\n**Historical context**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces (ARMOR, NEEDLE, AgentScribe, kalshi-weather, jedarden.com, vibe-coding-discovery, face/pose/sun repos) each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads in ARMOR (bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44) were permanently lost. This fix implements the flush-before-repair protection.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 3: CLI Commands\n\n### 3.1 Command Structure (`src/cli/`)\n\nUse `clap` with derive macros. Binary name: `bf`. Subcommands mirror br exactly.\n\n```\nbf create    --title \"...\" --type <type> --priority <N> [--description \"...\"] [--label ...]\nbf list      [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--limit N] [--format json|text|toon]\nbf show      <id>\nbf update    <id> [--status <s>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>] [--title \"...\"] ...\nbf close     <id> [--reason \"...\"]\nbf reopen    <id>\nbf delete    <id>\nbf ready         [--limit N]                     # SQLite's write lock is acquired before any reads, so no two workers can read the same candidate state. No flock, no server, no daemon.\n\n```\nWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT candidates → score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\nWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked at write lock until Worker 1 COMMITs) → SELECT → score → UPDATE → COMMIT\nWorker 3: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked) → ...\n...\nWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked) → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT (no-op)\n```\n\nEach claim is a single CLI invocation. The critical section (lock held) is: SELECT scoring fields → score in memory → UPDATE winner + stale resets → COMMIT. Lock held for ~0.5-2ms.\n\n**Throughput**: SQLite handles claims purely in memory after the initial page cache warm-up:\n\n| Workspace | Active beads | Claim latency | Throughput |\n|-----------|-------------|---------------|-----------|\n| Typical (FORGE) | 248 | ~0.5ms | ~2000/sec |\n| Medium (NEEDLE) | 518 | ~1ms | ~1000/sec |\n| Large | 2000 | ~2ms | ~500/sec |\n\nWith 20 workers claiming simultaneously, the last worker waits ~20-40ms (19 queued transactions × ~1-2ms each). The fleet needs ~1-2 claims/sec at steady state — SQLite is overkill by 3 orders of magnitude.\n\n### 4.2 Atomic Claim (`src/claim.rs`)\n\nThe entire claim sequence runs inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. }\n443\t    }\n444\t    reference.to_string()\n445\t}\n446\t\n447\tfn execute_create(\n448\t    tx: &Connection,\n449\t    title: &str,\n450\t    type_: &str,\n451\t    priority: i32,\n452\t created_ids.push(id.clone());\n561\t    Ok(id)\n562\t}\n563\t\n564\t/// Execute a dep_add_blocker operation (unified with CLI dep add command)\n565\t///\n566\t/// # Arguments\n567\t/// * `id` - The bead being blocked (must close after blocker closes)\n568\t/// * `blocker` - The bead that blocks (must close before id can close)\n569\t///\n570\t/// # Returns\n571\t/// * `Ok(())` if the dependency was added successfully\n572\t/// * `Err(...)` if validation fails (cycle, duplicate, missing beads)\n573\t///\n574\t/// # Direction\n575\t/// Creates: id depends on blocker (blocker blocks id)\n576\t/// This matches: `bf dep add <blocker> --blocks <id>`\n577\tfn execute_dep_add_blocker(tx: &Connection, id: &str, blocker: &str) -> Result<()> {\n578\t    // Verify both beads exist\n579\t    let id_exists: bool = tx.query_row(\n580\t        \"SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM issues WHERE id = ?1)\",\n581\t        &[id],\n582\t        |row| row.get(0),\n583\t    )?;\n584\t\n585\t    let blocker_exists: bool = tx.query_row(\n586\t        \"SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM issues WHERE id = ?1)\",\n587\t        &[blocker],\n588\t        |row| row.get(0),\n589\t    )?;\n590\t\n591\t    if !id_exists {\n592\t        return Err(anyhow!(\"Bead not found: {}\", id));\n593\t    }\n594\t    if !blocker_exists {\n595\t        return Err(anyhow!(\"Bead not found: {}\", blocker));\n596\t    }\n597\t\n598\t    // Check for duplicate dependency\n599\t    let exists: bool = tx.query_row(\n600\t        \"SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM dependencies WHERE issue_id = ?1 AND depends_on_id = ?2)\",\n601\t        &[id, blocker],\n602\t        |row| row.get(0),\n603\t    )?;\n604\t\n605\t    if exists {\n606\t        return Err(anyhow!(\n607\t            \"Dependency already exists: {} depends on {}\",\n608\t            id,\n609\t            blocker\n610\t        ));\n611\t    }\n612\t\n613\t    // Check for circular dependency (id -> blocker and blocker -> id)\n614\t    let reverse_exists: bool = tx.query_row(\n615\t        \"SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM dependencies WHERE issue_id = ?1 AND depends_on_id = ?2)\",\n616\t        &[blocker, id],\n617\t        |row| row.get(0),\n618\t    )?;\n619\t\n620\t    if reverse_exists {\n621\t        return Err(anyhow!(\n622\t            \"Circular dependency detected: {} <-> {}\",\n623\t            id,\n624\t            blocker\n625\t        ));\n626\t    }\n627\t\n628\t    // Add dependency (id depends on blocker, so blocker blocks id)\n629\t    let now = Utc::now();\n630\t    tx.execute(\n631\t        \"INSERT INTO dependencies (issue_id, depends_on_id, type, created_at, created_by)\n632\t         VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4, ?5)\",\n633\t        rusqlite::params![\n634\t            id,\n635\t            blocker,\n636\t            DependencyType::Blocks.to_string(),\n637\t            now.to_rfc3339(),\n638\t            \"batch\",\n639\t        ],\n640\t    )?;\n641\t\n642\t    // Both endpoints' exported records reflect the new edge; mark both dirty so\n643\t    // the end-of-transaction flush re-exports them.\n644\t    mark_dirty_tx(tx, id)?;\n645\t    mark_dirty_tx(tx, blocker)?;\n646\t\n647\t    Ok(())\n648\t}\n649\t\n650\tfn execute_close(tx: &Connection, id: &str, reason: &str) -> Result<()> {\n651\t    // Verify bead exists\n652\t    let exists: bool = tx.query_row(\n653\t        \"SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM issues WHERE id = ?1)\",\n654\t        &[id],\n655\t        |row| row.get(0),\n656\t    )?;\n657\t\n658\t    if !exists {\n659\t        return Err(anyhow!(\"Bead not found: {}\", id));\n660\t    }\n661\t\n662\t    // Check if already closed for idempotence\n663\t    let current_status: Option<String> = tx\n664\t        .query_row(\n665\t            \"SELECT status FROM issues WHERE id = ?1\",\n666\t            &[id],\n667\t            |row| row.get(0),\n668\t        )\n669\t        .ok();\n670\t\n671\t    if current_status.as_deref() == Some(\"closed\") {\n672\t        // Already closed - idempotent, return success\n673\t        return Ok(());\n674\t    }\n675\t\n676\t    let now = Utc::now();\n677\t    tx.execute(\n678\t        \"UPDATE issues SET status = 'closed', closed_at = ?, close_reason = ?, updated_at = ?\n679\t         WHERE id = ?\",\n680\t        rusqlite::params![now.to_rfc3339(), reason, now.to_rfc3339(), id],\n681\t    )?;\n682\t\n683\t    tx.execute(\n684\t        \"INSERT INTO events (issue_id, event_type, actor, old_value, new_value, created_at)\n685\t         VALUES (?1, 'closed', '', '', ?2, ?3)\",\n686\t        rusqlite::params![id, reason, now.to_rfc3339()],\n687\t    )?;\n688\t\n689\t    // Mark the just-closed bead dirty for the end-of-transaction flush.\n690\t    mark_dirty_tx(tx, id)?;\n691\t\n692\t    // Cascade status transition: find dependents that should move from blocked->open\n693\t    // A dependent should be unblocked if it has no remaining blockers in non-terminal status\n694\t    let dependents: Vec<(String, String)> = tx\n695\t        .prepare(\n696\t            \"SELECT d.issue_id, i.status\n697\t             FROM dependencies d\n698\t             INNER JOIN issues i ON i.id = d.issue_id\n699\t             WHERE d.depends_on_id = ?1\n700\t             AND d.type IN ('blocks', 'parent-child', 'conditional-blocks', 'waits-for')\",\n701\t        )?\n702\t        .query_map(&[id], |row| {\n703\t            Ok((row.get::<_, String>(0)?, row.get::<_, String>(1)?))\n704\t        })?\n705\t        .collect::<std::result::Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;\n706\t\n707\t    for (dep_id, dep_status) in dependents {\n708\t        // Only transition beads currently at status='blocked'\n709\t        if dep_status != \"blocked\" {\n710\t            continue;\n711\t        }\n712\t\n713\t        // Check if the dependent has any OTHER remaining blockers not in terminal status\n714\t        let remaining_blockers: i64 = tx\n715\t            .query_row(\n716\t                r#\"\n717\t                SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT d.depends_on_id)\n718\t                FROM dependencies d\n719\t                INNER JOIN issues i ON i.id = d.depends_on_id\n720\t                WHERE d.issue_id = ?1\n721\t                AND d.type IN ('blocks', 'parent-child', 'conditional-blocks', 'waits-for')\n722\t                AND i.status NOT IN ('closed', 'tombstone', 'done', 'completed')\n723\t                \"#,\n724\t                &[&dep_id],\n725\t                |row| row.get(0),\n726\t            )\n727\t            .unwrap_or(0);\n728\t\n729\t        // If no remaining blockers, transition to 'open'\n730\t        if remaining_blockers == 0 {\n731\t            let now = Utc::now();\n732\t            tx.execute(\n733\t                \"UPDATE issues SET status = 'open', updated_at = ?1 WHERE id = ?2\",\n734\t                rusqlite::params![now.to_rfc3339(), &dep_id],\n735\t            )?;\n736\t            tx.execute(\n737\t                \"INSERT INTO events (issue_id, event_type, actor, old_value, new_value, created_at) VALUES (?1, 'status_changed', 'system', 'blocked', 'open', ?2)\",\n738\t                rusqlite::params![&dep_id, now.to_rfc3339()],\n739\t            )?;\n740\t            // A cascaded blocked->open transition changes the dependent's\n741\t            // exported status; mark it dirty too.\n742\t            mark_dirty_tx(tx, &dep_id)?;\n743\t        }\n744\t    }\n745\t\n746\t    // Rebuild blocked_issues_cache to reflect the new blocker state\n747\t    tx.execute(\"DELETE FROM blocked_issues_cache\", [])?;\n748\t    tx.execute(\n749\t        \"INSERT INTO blocked_issues_cache (issue_id, blocked_by, blocked_at)\n750\t         SELECT d.issue_id, '[' || GROUP_CONCAT('\\\"' || d.depends_on_id || '\\\"') || ']' AS blocked_by, ?1\n751\t         FROM dependencies d\n752\t         INNER JOIN issues i ON i.id = d.depends_on_id\n753\t         WHERE d.type IN ('blocks', 'parent-child', }\n1064\t\n1065\t    // Add dependencies: each child blocks the parent\n1066\t    // Reference children by placeholder (@0, @1, etc.)\n1067\t    for (idx, _) in children.iter().enumerate() {\n1068\t execute_dep_add_blocker(tx: &Connection, id: &str, blocker: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    // Verify both beads exist\n    let id_exists: bool = tx.query_row(\n        \"SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM issues WHERE id = ?1)\",\n        &[id],\n        |row| row.get(0),\n    )?;\n\n    let blocker_exists: bool = tx.query_row(\n        \"SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM issues WHERE id = ?1)\",\n        &[blocker],\n        |row| row.get(0),\n    )?;\n\n    if !id_exists {\n        return Err(anyhow!(\"Bead not found: {}\", id));\n    }\n    if !blocker_exists {\n        return Err(anyhow!(\"Bead not found: {}\", blocker));\n    }\n\n    // Check for duplicate dependency\n    let exists: bool = tx.query_row(\n        \"SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM dependencies WHERE issue_id = ?1 AND depends_on_id = ?2)\",\n        &[id, blocker],\n        |row| row.get(0),\n    )?;\n\n    if exists {\n        return Err(anyhow!(\n            \"Dependency already exists: {} depends on {}\",\n            id,\n            blocker\n        ));\n    }\n\n    // Check for circular dependency (id -> blocker and blocker -> id)\n    let reverse_exists: bool = tx.query_row(\n        \"SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM dependencies WHERE issue_id = ?1 AND depends_on_id = ?2)\",\n        &[blocker, id],\n        |row| row.get(0),\n    )?;\n\n    if reverse_exists {\n        return Err(anyhow!(\n            \"Circular dependency detected: {} <-> {}\",\n            id,\n            blocker\n        ));\n    }\n\n    // Add dependency (id depends on blocker, so blocker blocks id)\n    let now = Utc::now();\n    tx.execute(\n        \"INSERT INTO dependencies (issue_id, depends_on_id, type, created_at, created_by)\n         VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4, ?5)\",\n        rusqlite::params![\n            id,\n            blocker,\n            DependencyType::Blocks.to_string(),\n            now.to_rfc3339(),\n            \"batch\",\n        ],\n    )?;\n\n    // Both endpoints' exported records reflect the new edge; mark both dirty so\n    // the end-of-transaction flush re-exports them.\n    mark_dirty_tx(tx, id)?;\n    mark_dirty_tx(tx, blocker)?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn execute_close(tx: &Connection, id: &str, reason: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    // Verify bead exists\n    let exists: bool = tx.query_row(\n        \"SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM issues WHERE id = ?1)\",\n        &[id],\n        |row| row.get(0),\n    )?;\n\n    if !exists {\n        return Err(anyhow!(\"Bead not found: {}\", id));\n    }\n\n    // Check if already closed for idempotence\n    let current_status: Option<String> = tx\n        .query_row(\n            \"SELECT status FROM issues WHERE id = ?1\",\n            &[id],\n            |row| row.get(0),\n        )\n        .ok();\n\n    if current_status.as_deref() == Some(\"closed\") {\n        // Already closed - idempotent, return success\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let now = Utc::now();\n    tx.execute(\n        \"UPDATE issues SET status = 'closed', closed_at = ?, close_reason = ?, updated_at = ?\n         WHERE id = ?\",\n        rusqlite::params![now.to_rfc3339(), reason, now.to_rfc3339(), id],\n    )?;\n\n    tx.execute(\n        \"INSERT INTO events (issue_id, event_type, actor, old_value, new_value, created_at)\n         VALUES (?1, 'closed', '', '', ?2, ?3)\",\n        rusqlite::params![id, reason, now.to_rfc3339()],\n    )?;\n\n    // Mark the just-closed bead dirty for the end-of-transaction flush.\n    mark_dirty_tx(tx, id)?;\n\n    // Cascade status transition: find dependents that should move from blocked->open\n    // A dependent should be unblocked if it has no remaining blockers in non-terminal status\n    let dependents: Vec<(String, String)> = tx\n        .prepare(\n            \"SELECT d.issue_id, i.status\n             FROM dependencies d\n             INNER JOIN issues i ON i.id = d.issue_id\n             WHERE d.depends_on_id = ?1\n             AND d.type IN ('blocks', 'parent-child', 'conditional-blocks', 'waits-for')\",\n        )?\n        .query_map(&[id], |row| {\n            Ok((row.get::<_, String>(0)?, row.get::<_, String>(1)?))\n        })?\n        .collect::<std::result::Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;\n\n    for (dep_id, dep_status) in dependents {\n        // Only transition beads currently at status='blocked'\n        if dep_status != \"blocked\" {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check if the dependent has any OTHER remaining blockers not in terminal status\n        let remaining_blockers: i64 = tx\n            .query_row(\n                r#\"\n                SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT d.depends_on_id)\n                FROM dependencies d\n                INNER JOIN issues i ON i.id = d.depends_on_id\n                WHERE d.issue_id = ?1\n                AND d.type IN ('blocks', 'parent-child', 'conditional-blocks', 'waits-for')\n                AND i.status NOT IN ('closed', 'tombstone', 'done', 'completed')\n                \"#,\n                &[&dep_id],\n                |row| row.get(0),\n            )\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n\n        // If no remaining blockers, transition to 'open'\n        if remaining_blockers == 0 {\n            let now = Utc::now();\n            tx.execute(\n                \"UPDATE issues SET status = 'open', updated_at = ?1 WHERE id = ?2\",\n                rusqlite::params![now.to_rfc3339(), &dep_id],\n            )?;\n            tx.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO events (issue_id, event_type, actor, old_value, new_value, created_at) VALUES (?1, 'status_changed', 'system', 'blocked', 'open', ?2)\",\n                rusqlite::params![&dep_id, now.to_rfc3339()],\n            )?;\n            // A cascaded blocked->open transition changes the dependent's\n            // exported status; mark it dirty too.\n            mark_dirty_tx(tx, &dep_id)?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Rebuild blocked_issues_cache to reflect the new blocker state\n    tx.execute(\"DELETE FROM blocked_issues_cache\", [])?;\n    tx.execute(\n        \"INSERT INTO blocked_issues_cache (issue_id, blocked_by, blocked_at)\n         SELECT d.issue_id, '[' || GROUP_CONCAT('\\\"' || d.depends_on_id || '\\\"') || ']' AS blocked_by, ?1\n         FROM dependencies d\n         INNER JOIN issues i ON i.id = d.depends_on_id\n         WHERE d.type IN ('blocks', 'parent-child', 'conditional-blocks', 'waits-for')\n         AND i.status NOT IN ('closed', 'tombstone', 'done', 'completed')\n         GROUP BY d.issue_id\",\n        rusqlite::params![Utc::now().to_rfc3339()],\n    )?;\n\n    // Invalidate critical path cache: closing a bead can unblock dependents\n    crate::critical_path::invalidate_cache(tx)?;\n    crate::critical_path::compute_all_critical_paths(tx)?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Execute an update operation\nfn execute_update(\n    tx: &Connection,\n    id: &str,\n    title: &Option<String>,\n    description: &Option<String>,\n    design: &Option<String>,\n    acceptance_criteria: &Option<String>,\n // Verify bead exists\n    let exists: bool = tx\n        .query_row(\n            \"SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM issues WHERE id = ?1)\",\n            &[id],\n            |row| row.get(0),\n
